title: Reference forms require an available local antecedent
summary: Test whether candidate reference-like wholes occur only when a compatible antecedent is available in the same bounded record, separating anaphoric use from a portable temporal or lexical reading.

design.mechanism: A reference whole points to an active prior item or result in the same record window; it is not freely inserted without an antecedent.
design.unit: exact candidate occurrences with the preceding two fields and their typed source/result roles
design.contrast: candidate occurrence with a compatible antecedent versus matched occurrence lacking one, stratified by register
design.prediction: Reference candidates show a higher rate of compatible antecedents and continuation slots, with the effect surviving register and line position; a temporal/lexical model predicts no antecedent dependency.
design.falsifier: No antecedent-rate difference on held records, or the effect is wholly explained by register/position, falsifies the bounded anaphoric mechanism.
design.scope: cached admitted records and existing typed role annotations; feasibility_unknown for independent antecedent coding
design.related: OLOR identity peer review retains temporal versus anaphoric rivals; this proposal tests antecedent availability, not reading robustness or negative contexts
